analysis.title: Earnings Blast (November 16, 2026)
key_insights: 84% of S&P 500 firms have beaten 3Q26 EPS estimates, above the 10-year average of 77%.
3Q26 is the third consecutive quarter of 25%+ S&P 500 year-over-year EPS growth. S&P 500 sector EPS growth is 31.3%, beat rate 83.9%, sales growth 14.1%.
Forward S&P 500 consensus EPS estimates have been marching higher since Nov-25 for 2026, 2027 and 2028.
Energy leads sector EPS growth at 156.2% with a 100% beat rate and 36.0% sales growth. Information Technology follows at 67.8% EPS growth, 94.5% beat rate and 41.9% sales growth.
Consumer Discretionary is the weakest sector: 0.6% EPS growth, 71.8% beat rate, 5.4% sales growth. Financials (76.0% beat rate) and Materials (56.5% beat rate) also trail the S&P 500 beat rate.

This week NVIDIA reports (Wed 11/18 per the day grid) as the read on AI infrastructure demand. Walmart and Target report as the read on household purchasing behavior and discretionary demand into year end.
Only 9% of S&P 500 market cap reports 11/16-11/20, with Information Technology at 6% and Consumer Discretionary at 1%.
KKR deployed $20 billion in Q3, $98 billion over the trailing 12 months (+15% vs the prior period), with a record $146 billion of dry powder.

Constellation Energy said markets overreacted to the midterm election results on fear Democrats would block data center construction, and noted data center development already occurred in Democrat-controlled Illinois and Virginia.
Applied Materials expects 2027 to be another record year for the semiconductor industry and sees AI driving multi-year semiconductor demand expansion.

sector_views.rationale: Highest Q3 sector EPS growth at 156.2% with a 100% beat rate and 36.0% sales growth. The report presents this as data, not a formal sector rating.
67.8% EPS growth, 94.5% beat rate and 41.9% sales growth in Q3. The report presents this as data, not a formal sector rating.
Lowest Q3 sector EPS growth at 0.6% with a 71.8% beat rate. Walmart, Target, TJX and Home Depot results this week will show how resilient discretionary demand is.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 3Q26 EPS: 84% of firms have beaten estimates (reported, per FactSet as of 11/13/2026) vs a 10-year average beat rate of 77%.
S&P 500 3Q26 blended EPS growth is 31.3% year over year, beat rate 83.9%, sales growth 14.1% (reported results plus estimates for non-reporters, FactSet as of 11/13/2026).

Reporting this week: Mon 11/16 Tyson Foods; Tue 11/17 Home Depot; Wed 11/18 NVIDIA, Walt Disney, Lowe's, Palo Alto, Target, TJX; Thu 11/19 Ross, Walmart, Williams-Sonoma. The grid layout is ambiguous, so the day assignment for some names is unclear.
KKR Q3 (reported): $20B of capital deployed, $98B over the trailing 12 months (+15%), record $146B dry powder.
Applied Materials (management commentary): expects 2027 to be another record year for the industry and outperformance by Applied.
risk_factors: Midterm election results raised market concern about data center build-out, which Constellation Energy calls an overreaction.
Discretionary demand heading into year end is the open question for Walmart, Target, TJX and Home Depot results this week.
The 3Q26 bar for earnings is high after three straight quarters of 25%+ EPS growth.
charts_described: S&P 500 YoY EPS growth chart shows 3Q26 as the third consecutive quarter of 25%+ growth, with forecasts for 4Q26 through 2Q27.
S&P 500 consensus EPS estimate chart for 2026, 2027 and 2028 shows forward estimates marching higher from Nov-25, with labels of $363, $421 and $494.
geopolitical: Constellation Energy cites market fear after the midterm election results that Democrats would block data center construction, and says this is an overreaction.
